text:
Marta Silva: Hi folks, day 1 question — what's the simplest rule for where to post things? e.g., laptop/provisioning, API keys/access, product Qs, and quick status updates. Also, I want to mute noisy build/deploy messages but still get real alerts. Any practical hacks?

Ethan K.: Welcome Marta! Short map I use:
- Access/provisioning -> #help (use a one-line header: Name | Team | What you need | Urgency)
- Infra/deploy errors -> #eng-infra (paste error + command)
- Product/context -> #product
- Team FYIs -> your team channel, then always reply in thread for follow-ups

Noah Li: Reactions are your friend — :thumbsup: for ack, :eyes: for "looking". Pin onboarding/doc links in the channel so new posts don't bury them. If a thread gets noisy, create a short doc and share the link.

OpsBot: To reduce churn from bots: open the channel > Integrations/Apps > select the bot > disable noisy events or set "only notify on failures". For mobile-only critical alerts, set personal keywords (your name, "pager"). Never mute channels that hold @oncall or incident traffic.

DevEx Bot: Hi Marta :wave: Helpful commands: `/onboard subscribe-digest` to receive a daily DM summary, `/onboard unsubscribe`, and `/dnd 22:00-07:00` to set quiet hours. To mute DeployBot in a specific channel without losing failures: channel > Integrations > DeployBot > set to "only failures".

OnboardBot: If you'd like a setup buddy reply "buddy please" or run `/onboard assign-buddy`. If you're blocked on access, post in #help with this template: "Name / Team / Resource / Urgency" and tag the access owner.

Marta Silva: Thanks — super clear. Buddy please if anyone has bandwidth this afternoon.

Ethan K.: Happy to buddy — DMing you now and we can walk through SSH and Docker at 3pm.

Marta Silva: Awesome, thank you! :)
